rendered:
The LLTO-2 coating retained the most capacity after 200[1] cycles when cycled at 0.5C[2]: it kept 86.2%[3] of its initial discharge capacity. The other LLTO coatings retained 85.5%[4] (LLTO-0.5) and 57.2%[5] (LLTO-1). By comparison, the pristine NCM retained only 56.6%[6] of its initial discharge capacity after 200[7] cycles, so the LLTO-2 coated NCM held far more capacity than the uncoated material.

Why the rate capability fell with the 2 mol.% coating[8]: the authors attribute it to a thicker coating layer. They say the rate capability decreased, which may be due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, and that this thickness suppresses the electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.[9][10]
